BrochureContent.Content:
COMMERCIAL UNIT WITH OVERHEAD ACCOMMODATION JUST OFF MARKET SQUARE KILDARE TOWN

Derelict Terraced Property In Need of Significant Renovation And Investment. 
Site extends to approx. 0.0136 hectares. 

In a prime location, this expended two storey traditional town property offers enormous opportunity for a mix of residential/commercial uses. 

The property comprises a two storey building that extends in total to approx. 138 sqm and boasts two retail units on ground floor, and residential accommodation overhead.

Accommodation Briefly Comprises:
Ground floor shop unit (Bargain Store Unit) extends to approx. 288 sq ft.
Ground floor shop unit (Tattoo Unit) extends to approx. 216 sq ft.
Hall: with access to rear (I could not access) and with stairwell to first floor.
First Floor: bathroom, 4 rooms and store room.
All the accommodation is unhabitable and requires major investment.

Superb Development Opportunity 
Excellent Location Within walking distance of all amenities and services in Kildare Town Centre. 

The potential purchaser will be required to 
1. Substantially complete works on this property so as to render it non-derelict and 
2. Return it to residential use within 24-30 months from the closing of the sale. 
3. There will be a buyback option for the council should the works not be completed within the required timeframe. 

Please review the Special Condition on the Contract 
https://kildarecoco.ie/AllServices/Housing/RegenerationandVacantHomes/VacantpropertyRefurbishmentGrant/ 
Please note special condition clause on contract: 
15. In the event that there has been no development of the subject property, in accordance with the terms of any Planning permission if applicable within a period of 18/24/30 calendar months from the closing date of this Contract or such further period thereafter as the Vendor may allow. The Vendor at its sole discretion shall have an option to request that the subject property be transferred back to the Vendor subject to the Purchaser being refunded the purchase price as per this Contract less 10% being a contribution to the Vendor's costs, i.e. 90% of the purchase price only shall be discharged to the Purchaser without any other interest, costs, or compensation. This clause shall be included in the Deed of Transfer to the Purchaser on closing and shall be registered as a burden on the Title to the property in sale. Once the property has been developed to the satisfaction of the Vendor, the Vendor through their Solicitors shall then execute a discharge of the burden on Title at no further expense to the Purchaser herein.

The property is located at Market Square in the town centre of Kildare. Kildare Town has its origins as a monastic settlement, dating back to the 5th century and evolved from its medieval past into a market town owing to its location and trade routes.

The population of the Kildare was 10,302 according to the latest 2022 census of population.

Kildare is situated 52 kilometres southwest of Dublin and is located adjacent to the north of the M7 motorway halfway between Monasterevin and Newbridge (An Droichead Nua) and is located at the fringe of The Curragh. 

Other neighbouring towns include Athy (19km away) and Naas (18km away). The town also has connections by rail to Cork, Dublin, Limerick and Waterford lines.

The town centre core has a variety of uses which include residential and commercial uses. 

These uses occupy mostly terraced buildings which face onto the Market Square.

This is also the case for the buildings occupied on Claregate Street and Bride Street.

Market Square is located in the town centre of Kildare Town, Co. Kildare. 

It is crossed diagonally by Bride Street in an east / southwest manner and bound by the Dublin Road (R446) to the south. 

St Brigid's Cathedral is located immediately to the northwest of the site. 

The location of the Square is central to the town, with the Square acting as its historic and present day focal point for a range of community and commercial activities and events. Market square hosts the weekly town market.

Surrounding uses are typical of town centres, with commercial services, the Heritage Centre and Tourist Office, comparison and convenience shops, restaurants, cafés and pubs, takeaways. 

Some buildings have different upper floor uses with limited residential accommodation and professional services such as solicitors. 

The Kildare train station is located around 650m north of the Square and Kildare Tourist Outlet Village is located around 1.5 km south of the subject site. 

The Dublin Road (R445) which bounds the Square to the south, links the town to Newbridge, the Curragh and the M7 to the east and to Monasterevin to the west. 

Prior to the opening of the M7, this road was a major axis between Dublin and Portlaoise. Bride Street (R415) splits the Square into two parts. 

It links Kildare town to the Rathbride townland to the north and to Nurney village to the south.

Most the buildings around the square itself date from the second half of the 18th century and the 19th century, meaning Market Square has retained much of its character.
